neet_che_u17_t08_1.working: HCHO has no electron-releasing alkyl groups and the least steric hindrance, so its carbonyl carbon is the most electrophilic and accessible.

neet_che_u17_t08_2.working: -NO2 withdraws electrons and raises carbonyl electrophilicity. -CH3 donates weakly (+I/hyperconjugation). -OCH3 donates strongly (+R). Order: P > B > T > M.

neet_che_u17_t08_3.working: In benzaldehyde the ring conjugates with C=O and donates electron density by resonance, lowering the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon. Option 3 is wrong (α-H is irrelevant to nucleophilic attack) and option 4 is wrong (propanal has only one alkyl group on the carbonyl carbon).

neet_che_u17_t08_4.working: A is true: acetaldehyde has one alkyl group and less steric hindrance than acetone. R is false: methyl groups are electron-releasing and reduce the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon.

neet_che_u17_t08_5.working: I is incorrect: bulky tert-butyl groups add steric hindrance and release electrons, both of which reduce reactivity. II is correct: the +I/hyperconjugative effect of -CH3 lowers carbonyl electrophilicity.
